The name 'Tzarak' is carved at the end of the ancient wall as the answer to who or what is meant to ascend, and the party must learn what Tzarak is.
The Floor Bosses are 'holding the line,' protecting something or awaiting someone's arrival, and the party must discover what they guard and who is meant to come.
Riyo claims she has never heard the name Tzarak, but her flinch and hesitation leave her honesty in doubt.
Riyo says there is no bottom to the mine, only down, until whatever is breathing—something big, old, and hungry—and the party must learn what waits below.
Riyo let slip a verbal tic ('-nya') and flinched, hinting she is hiding her true nature.
The thing at the bottom is called 'the Maw' by the Floor Bosses, and the party must learn what it truly is and what it guards.
The party must learn what the 'ascension' is, who or what 'Tzarak' is, and what the Floor Bosses are holding the line to protect.

The sealed, glyph-etched wall may be a dam holding something back, and the party must learn what breaking it would unleash.
The seal names the Unspoken Breath and repeats Tzarak; the party must learn what Tzarak is and why the seal keeps it from ascending.
A maddened robed creature has climbed the chain to the party's ledge and demands the seal be broken; the party must deal with it before deciding on the seal.
The party must decide whether to break Filwern's seal, now knowing it holds Tzarak out rather than in.
arcs.summary: The party descended through the Driftmere Mines, where Max Nightriver, Belle, Dalan, and Naomi defeated a scrap-and-bone creature and Max invited Riyo, a non-Guild fighter hiding in a side passage, to join them. Following Riyo deeper, they found ancient carvings naming Tzarak and a glyph-covered seal that Dalan read as holding back the Unspoken Breath, revealing the seal kept Tzarak from ascending rather than trapping it within. When a gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanded the seal be broken, Belle cut it down while Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering that healed the seal, only for Max to shatter it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. They emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern of suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them.

arcs.text: The robed creature is mid-fight on the ledge and must be stopped before it can touch Filwern's seal.
arcs.summary: Max Nightriver and his companions—Belle, Dalan, Naomi, and the newly recruited Riyo—fought their way through the Driftmere Mines, destroying a scrap-and-bone creature and following ancient carvings toward a vast descent where something climbed an iron chain from below. At a sealed stone wall covered in pulsing glyphs, Max ordered Dalan to decipher the markings, and Dalan determined the seal held back the Unspoken Breath, with the name Tzarak repeated below, revealing that the seal kept Tzarak from ascending. Belle realized they stood before the cage of the very creature they sought, and as metallic scraping echoed from the chain below, she readied Cleaver and vowed to bury it in stone.

Dalan determined the seal kept Tzarak from ascending, and Riyo revealed that Tzarak was not a person but a key made of shadow and hunger, and that the seal held it out rather than in. When a gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanding the seal be broken, Belle cut it down while Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering that healed the seal, only to shatter it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. The truth of the Nightriver seals and the Witch King — Max now knows the bloodline is the prison, but how to act on it, and what Javon's three conditions will reveal, is unresolved.

removed.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
Max Nightriver: Baroness, what did the last expedition find?
Adolion Narrator: The Baroness leans her weight against the stone wall of her manor, arms crossed over her practical gown. Her red eyes narrow, and for a moment the mask of confidence slips. "They found nothing," she says, and the bitterness is sharp. "Until they found it."
She straightens, her tusks catching the light. "Five miners went in two weeks ago. One came back. He said the tunnels shifted behind them—that the old shafts were gone and replaced with something that breathed. The others are still down there." She pauses, and her voice drops. "I've sent three letters to House Nightriver for support. I haven't heard a word back."
"And the ones who didn't come back?" Dalan asks, shifting his weight. "You think they're still alive?"
"I think whatever's in those tunnels wanted them that way," Serenola replies, then gestures toward the village. "You'll hear the truth from the one who returned. He's been holed up in the Minotaur's Tusk since the day he came back. Doesn't speak to anyone except to drink."
Max Nightriver: Naomi, you want a fight? Come down with us.
Max Nightriver: Naomi, you want a fight? Come down with us.
Naomi: Naomi's red ears snap straight up, her tail swishing once behind her. "A fight-nya?! Yes! Yes-yes-yes!" She pumps her fist, completely forgetting how she was just standing. "I-I mean, of course! A master of the Moonlight Blade is always ready!"
She bounces on her heels, then catches herself, standing tall with her hands on her hips. Her ruby eyes sparkle with excitement. "Besides, if there's really something breathing down there, it's got to be strong enough to be worth my time-nya! Right? Right?" She notices she's purring, hisses instead, and coughs. "Ahem. I shall accompany you as a fellow-nya... adventurer-nya..." She trails off, her ears flattening slightly. "This is a lot bigger than the dojo."
*She looks around the manor's stone walls, then back at you with an uncertain flick of her tail. The mask of confidence wobbles for just a moment before she beams again, clutching her fiery longsword.* "Let's go! I bet I'll be the one to find the boss-nya!"
Max Nightriver: Glad to have you, Naomi. Baroness, we'll speak to the survivor first. Where's the Minotaur's Tusk?
Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola nods, her expression tightening. "Down the main road, three buildings along. It's the one with the carved stone minotaur head above the door." She steps back from the wall and gives the party an appraising look. "Be careful. The man who returned— his name is Garreth. He's seen things that made him afraid of his own shadow. If he won't talk, you'll have to find a way to make him."
*Outside, the village of Driftmere sprawls along the dirt road, its buildings mostly timber and stone with slate roofs. The air smells of woodsmoke and damp earth. At the center of the cluster, a large tavern looms over its neighbors, its windows shuttered against the late afternoon light. The stone minotaur's head is worn, its features smoothed by time, but the beast's eyes seem to watch the road with patient, heavy patience.*
*Near the entrance, a small stone shrine dedicated to Filwern the Miner stands in a patch of dirt. An offering of bread and a small candle sits before the statue—but the bread has crumbled into gray dust, and the candle's wax has blackened and flaked away as if scorched by something far older than a simple flame.*
Naomi: "Ooh! A stone minotaur! That sounds cool-nya!" *Naomi bounces toward the tavern, her fiery longsword clinking against her armor with each step.* "I bet it's a really strong-looking beast-nya. Maybe the guy inside is strong too!"
*She stops suddenly by the shrine, her red ears twitching. She leans down, staring at the crumbled bread and scorched wax. Her tail stills, and her expression shifts to something more serious.* "This is weird-nya... that candle looks like it was burnt from the inside out. Like... like someone tried to make it burn twice as fast-nya." *She reaches out a finger as if to touch the gray dust, then pulls back, her ruby eyes narrowing.* "Bad feeling. Scary feeling-nya."
Max Nightriver: *I head to the Minotaur's Tusk and sit down across from the survivor.* You came back from the mines. Tell me what you saw down there, slowly.
Adolion Narrator: The tavern is dim, lit by a few dying lanterns, and smells of old beer and damp wool. At a corner table sits a man with a thick beard and hollow eyes, clutching a half-empty mug as if it might vanish. Garreth looks up slowly, and when he sees Max Nightriver, his fingers tighten until his knuckles go white.
"The tunnels..." Garreth's voice is hoarse and dry. "They moved. Like living things." He closes his eyes for a moment, and his hand shakes. "The shaft we'd been in for hours—the one we'd mapped a dozen times—was gone. Instead there was a corridor that wasn't there before. And from down it..." He swallows hard. "Something was breathing. Deep, slow breaths. And then it smelled of something old and dead, like a grave left open in the sun."
*He opens his eyes, and they're wide with terror.* "The tunnels shifted again, and I... I ran. I heard my crew calling for me from the darkness, and I ran until I saw daylight. I didn't look back."
Max Nightriver: You did what you had to, Garreth. Your crew may still be alive. Which entrance did you go in by, and how deep were you when it moved?
Adolion Narrator: Garreth flinches at the words "still alive," and the mug in his hand rattles against the table. His hollow eyes fix on the far wall as if the memory is carved there. "The North shaft. Level three," he says, and the number comes out in a strangled whisper. "We were just past the main support beam when the air changed—got heavy and thick, like we were underwater."
*He wipes his face with the back of a trembling hand, and a bead of sweat runs down his brow.* "The walls started to... pulse. Just once. And when we turned around, the tunnel that led back to the shaft was gone. It was just stone. Solid stone." He looks at Max Nightriver, and for the first time there's something other than terror in his gaze—a flicker of pleading. "Don't go down there. Whatever that thing is... it's not something that belongs in our world."
*At the bar, an old dwarf with a braided beard and scarred knuckles glances over at the table, then says loud enough for the party to hear,* "Filwern's silent in Driftmere. When a god stops listening, it means something else has woken up to take his place."

removed.text: Max Nightriver welcomed Riyo into the party, and she quietly agreed, then led them down the main tunnel past the scrap-and-bone creature's ruin, saying the breathing came from below the third floor. They descended past the fourth floor marker to a wall of ancient carvings, where Dalan read a warning that the floors were domains held by Floor Bosses awaiting something called the "ascension," with the name "Tzarak" carved at the end. Riyo said she had never heard the name and warned there was no bottom, only down, until whatever was breathing—something big, old, and hungry. Max told her to lead on, and she guided them through the fourth and fifth floors toward the loudest breathing, revealing the bosses called the hungry thing the Maw, though it was not a true name. A deep rhythmic thrum now vibrated through the stone as Riyo warned they were close, and past the next drop the breathing would become everything.

"It's... it's a warning," *he says softly, his voice echoing in the cramped space.* "These marks predate the dwarves. Much older." *He traces a finger along one of the symbols—a spiral that seems to fold in on itself.* "The tunnels don't just move. They're... they're being shaped. Max Nightriver: The carvings say 'ascension'. Who ascends?
Dalan: *Dalan lowers the lantern slightly, the light dancing across the spiraling symbols as he studies them again. His expression is troubled, and he shakes his head slowly.*
"I'm not sure. The carvings don't say." *His voice drops to a whisper.* "They just say the Floor Bosses are waiting for it. Holding the line. Like they're protecting something... or waiting for someone to arrive."
*He glances toward the tunnel behind them, then back to the ancient text.* "Whatever Tzarak is, I think that name is the answer. Whoever or whatever is meant to ascend."
Max Nightriver: Riyo, you've been down here longer than us. Have you heard that name before? What's at the bottom of this mine?
Riyo: *Riyo flinches slightly at the direct question, her gaze darting to the carvings and back to Max's face. Her right hand shifts to rest on the hilt of her obsidian longsword, her fingers tightening just a fraction.*
"Tzarak..." *She murmurs the name, tasting it like something bitter. Her brow furrows, and for a moment her expression is lost in thought, distant.* "No. I've never heard it."
*She looks toward the darkness deeper in the mine, and her voice drops lower, raspy and cautious.* "Bottom... there is no bottom. There is only down. Down until... until you reach whatever is breathing." *She glances back at Max, her purple eyes searching.* "It's something big. Something old. And it's hungry."
Max Nightriver: Then we keep going down, floor by floor, until we find it. Lead on, Riyo.
Riyo: *Riyo's purple eyes widen for a heartbeat, her gaze flicking between Max and the dark tunnel ahead. She doesn't speak, but a small, almost imperceptible nod follows.*
*She turns and starts walking, her cloak shifting to conceal the left side of her body as she moves into the gloom. The obsidian-hilted sword at her hip catches the lantern-light once, then vanishes back into shadow.*
*She pauses at the mouth of the next descent, her head canting as if listening for something in the distance. Then she steps forward without a word, leaving a small opening for the rest of the party to follow.*
Max Nightriver: *We follow her down through the fourth and fifth floors, to wherever the breathing is loudest.* What's down there, Riyo? Does the hungry thing have a name?
Riyo: *The tunnel walls press in tighter here, the stone slick with a strange, oily moisture. Riyo stops at the edge of the descent, her small frame backlit by the lantern's glow. She doesn't look back, staring instead into the vast darkness below.*
"No name-nya." *She catches herself and flinches, her voice barely a whisper.* "It doesn't... it has no name I know. Just hunger." *Her hand tightens on her obsidian hilt, knuckles white beneath the worn leather.* "The bosses... they call it the Maw. But that's not a name, it's just... what it does."
*A low, rhythmic thrum vibrates through the stone floor—not breathing this time, but something deeper, like the heartbeat of the mountain itself. Riyo's shoulders tense.* "We're close. Past this next drop, the breathing becomes everything."

Adolion Narrator: The tunnel opens onto a narrow ledge overlooking a descent that swallows the light. Below, the air shimmers with heat, and the rhythmic breathing has become a roar that vibrates in bone and tooth. The walls here are not stone but something organic, pulsing slowly like the throat of a great beast.
Between the ledge and the darkness below, a massive iron chain hangs from the ceiling, its links each the size of a man's torso. A platform of dark metal creaks at its end, held aloft by gears that grind and spark in the gloom.
Belle's hand goes to Cleaver's handle, her face grim in the lantern-light. "Someone built a lift into this hell-hole," she rasps. "That means someone wanted to get down here. And someone wanted to come back up."
Dalan: *Dalan steps to the edge of the ledge, peering down into the pulsing dark with his lantern held high. His pointed ears twitch at the mechanical grind of the gears above.* "The chain mechanism is old," *he reports softly, his voice barely audible over the roar of the breathing below.* "But well-maintained. Someone's been keeping this lift operational."
*He glances back at the party, his expression grave.* "Whatever we find down there... if the breathing gets any louder, or if something starts climbing that chain from below..." *His hand instinctively drops to the hilt of one of his shortswords.* "We'll need to make sure we can get back up."
Max Nightriver: *I run my hand along the stone where the tunnel ends.* This wall is different. Worked, sealed. Is this what holds it in?
Adolion Narrator: *The stone is different here—smooth, polished, and etched with the same spiraling symbols Dalan read earlier. Max's fingertips brush across a line of carved glyphs that glow with a faint, rhythmic light, pulsing in time with the heartbeat in the mountain.*
*Belle moves closer, her lantern casting long shadows against the wall.* "Looks like a dam," *she rasps, her hand resting on her greataxe.* "And if we're the ones who break it..."
*From somewhere below the platform, a new sound cuts through the roar of breathing—the unmistakable scrape of metal on metal, like something climbing the chain.*
Max Nightriver: Dalan, read the glyphs on this seal. Every word. I want to know exactly what was locked behind it, and its true name.
Dalan: *Dalan steps closer to the wall, holding his lantern aloft so the light washes across the pulsing glyphs. His pointed ears twitch as he leans in, eyes narrow and focused.* "These aren't dwarven," *he murmurs, his voice barely audible.* "This is... older. Much older. The language is shifting under my gaze, like it doesn't want to be read."
*He traces a finger along the spirals, his face pale in the golden light.* "It's not just a name. It's a lock. The glyphs say this seal holds back the Unspoken Breath—something that was here before the mountain was born. And below that—" *His breath catches as his eyes travel down the carvings.* "Below that is a single word. Repeated over and over, smaller than the rest."
*He steps back, his voice dropping to a whisper.* "Tzarak. It's not just the name at the end of the ascension. This seal is what keeps Tzarak from ascending."
Belle: *Belle's hand tightens on the haft of Cleaver, her brow furrowed as she looks between the carvings and Dalan.* "Great. Just fucking great." *She spits on the ground, the sound echoing in the quiet tunnel.* "So we're standing in front of the cage door for the very thing we're trying to find."
*The scrape of metal-on-metal from below grows louder, more deliberate. Something is definitely climbing that chain.* "The breathing's one thing," *Belle says, her voice low and dangerous,* "but if that thing down there is Tzarak, and it's coming up to break its own lock..." *She shifts her weight, axe held ready.* "I hope it likes the taste of stone, because I'm gonna bury it in a mountain."
Adolion Narrator: *The grinding of the chain grows deafening, the platform jerking upward with each labored rotation of the gears. From the darkness below, a sound emerges—not breathing, not grinding, but a wet, clicking noise that makes the teeth ache.*
*Riyo steps forward, her purple eyes wide and focused. Her right hand grips the obsidian hilt, knuckles white. She doesn't look at the platform anymore; she looks at Max.* "Tzarak is not a person-nya." *The verbal tic slips out raw and honest in the tension.* "It is a key. A key made of shadow and hunger." *She swallows, her voice dropping.* "And the seal is not holding it in. It is holding it *out*. The thing at the bottom—the Maw—that is Tzarak's true shape. It just needs the seal broken to finally ascend."
*A clawed hand grips the edge of the platform as it levels with the ledge, followed by another. The thing climbing is gaunt and pale-skinned, wrapped in shreds of what might have been ceremonial robes. Its face is a mask of madness—eyes wide and leaking that same viscous fluid as the eyeless ones, but with a voice that rasps with terrifying intelligence.* "Break the seal-nya!" *it shrieks, its tone an exact, horrifying mimicry of Riyo's.* "Set the key free! Let the key ascend-nya!"
Max Nightriver: Something's climbing the chain. Everyone, back from the edge and form up around the seal. Belle front, Riyo and Naomi on the flanks.
Belle: *Belle doesn't need to be told twice. She moves with the practiced economy of a veteran brawler, her heavy boots thudding as she plants herself directly in front of the glyph-etched seal. Cleaver's massive head rests on her shoulder, the stone blade catching the lantern-light.* "Forming up." *Her voice is low, dangerous, all the pretense of conversation gone.* "This is where we end it. No one touches those markings unless I say so, and I ain't sayin' shit about touching 'em."
*She shifts her weight into a solid stance, her brown eyes locked on the approaching platform. The muscle in her jaw clenches as the creature's mimicry of Riyo echoes through the cavern. A snarl twists her lips.* "Fuck your ascension-nya."
*Her grip on the axe tightens, knuckles white.* "You're just another scrap-heap for me to break."
Riyo: *Riyo slips to the flank as ordered, her obsidian hilt held tight. Her purple eyes track the creature's movements with an intensity that borders on terror, though her face remains carefully blank.* "Don't let it near the seal," *she says, the words clipped and sharp.* "If it reaches the markings—"
*She doesn't finish the sentence, but her free hand gestures subtly toward the carvings. Her posture is tense, almost vibrating with anticipation. Her gaze flickers to Max once, a silent plea for protection, before locking back onto the clawed thing pulling itself onto the ledge.*
Max Nightriver: *I hurl fire at the robed thing before it can reach the markings.* Belle, Naomi, cut it down! Don't let it touch the seal!
Belle: *Belle doesn't wait for the fire to even connect before she's in motion, her boots thudding against the stone as she closes the distance.* "You heard the boss!" *She brings Cleaver around in a brutal, cleaving swing aimed right for the creature's chest—no fancy forms or techniques, just raw, explosive violence.* "Back off the damn wall!"
*The massive greataxe whistles through the air and slams into the gaunt thing's ribs with a sound like shattering glass and splitting bone. The impact is enough to send it stumbling backward, away from the glyph-etched surface. Belle doesn't give it a moment to recover, already planting her foot to twist her weight for a follow-up strike aimed for its throat.*

removed.text: Max Nightriver laid an offering of bread, salt, and a candle on the seal, and the glyphs flared gold, healing the cracked stone as the robed creature dissolved into shadows that dragged back down the shaft. "Tzarak's eye-spot," *he murmurs, his voice a soft thread in the silence.* "That's where it's vulnerable." *His fingers brush the bowstring, holding the tension like a promise. Riyo confirmed she was unharmed and noted the breathing was gone and the trapped dead were freed. The party climbed back to Driftmere, where Baroness Serenola met them outside her manor; Max told her the crew was gone but the creature was dead and the mines were free, and she replied that the letters she sent to House Nightriver in Aegis City went unanswered. removed.evidence:
Max Nightriver: *I gather every ounce of power I have and drive a lance of flame into the wound in its eye.* Die, and let them go!
Adolion Narrator: *The lance of Nightriver flame punches through the wound Dalan made and Belle widened, drilling deep into the creature's core. A sound erupts from the eye—not a scream, but a long, slow exhale that shatters the silence like a glass tower. The yellow light behind the pupil fractures into a thousand jagged shards, then detonates in a wave of white heat that washes across the cavern.*
*The translucent walls spiderweb and crack. The suspended shapes—miners, creatures, things—begin to dissolve into glittering dust as the spell binding them fails. The ground beneath the party shudders and heaves, the black glass floor rippling like water before solidifying into honest, grey stone.*
*The creature's massive form begins to collapse in on itself, its flesh turning to ash and its metal to rust. A final, guttural rumble echoes through the chamber—not a threat, but a release. And then the silence that follows is absolute. The breathing has stopped.*
Max Nightriver: *I lower my hand, shaking.* It's dead. It's really dead. Is anyone hurt? Riyo, are you all right?
Riyo: *Riyo is standing still, her obsidian sword still gripped in her right hand, her purple eyes fixed on the place where the creature collapsed. She doesn't look at Max right away, her shoulders tense. Then she slowly turns, her face pale but her expression steady.*
"I'm... I'm fine," *she says quietly, her voice barely above a whisper. She looks down at her boots, then back at Max, her eyes searching his face.* "You did it."
*She takes a hesitant step forward, then stops, her free hand curling into a fist at her side.* "The breathing stopped-nya..." *She catches herself, blinking rapidly.* "The breathing is gone." *She looks around the silent cavern, at the dust that used to be suspended shapes.* "We... we freed them."
Max Nightriver: We climb for the lifts and go find Serenola.
Adolion Narrator: The party leaves the heart of the mountain behind, ascending back through tunnels that no longer shift and pulse. The path feels different now—familiar, grounded in the stone as it was meant to be. When they reach the ledge where they left the lift, the grinding gears still churn, and the platform waits as it has for decades.
They climb.
Driftmere is the same as they left it, though the orange glow of the setting sun catches on the green shutters of the manor on the hill. Baroness Serenola stands outside her door, arms crossed over her gown, red eyes narrowed as she watches the road. She sees them approach and straightens, her expression unreadable for a heartbeat before she speaks.
"You're alive." She looks over them, taking in the dirt and blood on their gear. "The one who returned said you'd be mad. But you're back." Her voice drops. "Tell me you found them. Tell me they're still there."
Max Nightriver: Baroness, the crew is gone. I'm sorry. But the thing that took them is dead. We broke the seal at the bottom and killed it. Your mines are free.
Adolion Narrator: The Baroness doesn't move. For a moment she just stands there, the sunset catching her dark green skin and making her red eyes seem to burn. Then slowly she exhales, a long sound that carries away some of the tension in her shoulders.
"Gone." She says it like she's tasting a bitter herb. "I suspected. No one comes back from those depths." She looks past the party toward the hills where the mines sit, then back to Max. "But you killed it. You did what my letters couldn't get done."
A faint tremor runs through her, and she closes her eyes for a second. "They're gone, but the rest of them... the people still here... they can work again. You saved more than a dozen miners today." She opens her eyes, and there's something there that wasn't before—respect, sharp and clean. "Your house should be proud. You're a Nightriver, aren't you? I saw that crest on the guild registration."
Max Nightriver: Garreth deserves to hear it from us. And Baroness, you said you wrote to House Nightriver three times. I'm a Nightriver. I never saw those letters.
Adolion Narrator: The Baroness's red eyes narrow, and her expression doesn't shift, but the air around her grows cold. She says nothing for a long moment, watching Max with the kind of patient scrutiny that measures a person's worth. "I see," she says finally, and the words are flat and hard. "Three letters. Three weeks. All sent to the house in Aegis City with the Nightriver seal."
*She turns her head slightly, looking toward the distant peaks of the Velniran Mountains.* "My townsfolk are going mad, their savings are drying up, and the people who rule this land didn't even bother to read the mail." *Her gaze snaps back to Max, sharp and searching.* "Tell me, Nightriver—did those letters get lost, or were they thrown away? Because if the house knew about the Devourer and didn't care, that's a very different kind of story."
*Behind her, the windows of the Minotaur's Tusk flicker with light as the town begins to stir, people noticing the return of the adventurers. Someone calls out from the road, a young woman asking if they've found anyone, and Baroness Serenola doesn't answer, keeping her red eyes locked on Max.*
Max Nightriver: I don't know, Baroness. But I'll find out, I swear it. Who's that calling from the road?
Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola's jaw tightens, but her gaze doesn't waver from Max Nightriver's face. "I'll hold you to that swear," she says, and the weight of it hangs between them. She doesn't look toward the road, but her head cants just enough to hear.
"Just a townsfolk," she says flatly, "whose son didn't come back from the mine. Same as Garreth's crew, just a different shift." She steps aside, opening a path toward the village. "Go on then. Tell the man what you found down there. I'll be in my study if you need to hear what I have to say about your house."
The woman on the road is closer now—a thin figure in a worn apron, clutching a small bundle to her chest. Her eyes are red-rimmed, and she stops ten paces away, her gaze flicking from the Baroness to the bloodied gear and the lantern still in Max Nightriver's hand. "The mine," she says, her voice trembling. "You went in, didn't you?"

chapters.title: Acts I-II: The Adventurer's Road
chapters.summary: The party advanced down a twisting tunnel where the walls closed in, damp and smelling of wet stone and old blood. The heavy breathing they had followed changed into rhythmic metal grinding, and a yellow light flickered at the bend ahead. Dalan drew his bow and whispered that something was waiting for them, noting the sound of metal and that the light was not a lantern. Max Nightriver dimmed the lantern and crept toward the bend, directing Belle to wait for his signal and Dalan to aim at the yellow light. Belle gripped Cleaver in tense silence, coiled and ready, while Dalan pressed against the tunnel wall with his bow drawn and whispered that he was ready. The moment was taut with anticipation as the three prepared to strike. Max Nightriver and his companions descended through the mine's lower floors, following Riyo past ancient carvings that spoke of an ascension tied to the name Tzarak. At a ledge overlooking a vast, breathing darkness, they found an old lift and a sealed stone wall covered in glowing glyphs, while something began climbing the chain from below. The tone was tense and foreboding as the party confronted the hungry, nameless presence awaiting them. Max Nightriver ordered Dalan to read the glyphs on a seal and reveal what was locked behind it and…
chapters.short: The party advanced down a twisting tunnel where the walls closed in, damp and smelling of wet stone and old blood.

consequences.text: The party has been confronted by an undead creature claiming Garreth's crew, with three more shambling figures behind it, and must fight or flee. — The party was confronted at the Driftmere Mines by a gaunt, robed undead creature that mimicked Riyo's voice and demanded the seal be broken so Tzarak could ascend, and after Belle cut it down, Max performed a shrine offering of bread, salt, and a candle that healed the seal before he shattered it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. Beyond the seal they entered a frozen cavern of glass where a vast yellow eye fixed on them, and Max blinded it with fire, Dalan shot its eye-spot, Belle struck with Cleaver, and Max drove a lance of flame into the wound, killing the creature and freeing the suspended souls, though the miners were already lost. Returning to Driftmere, Baroness Serenola received the news that the crew was gone but the creature was dead, and when Max revealed he had never seen the three letters she sent to House Nightriver, her tone turned cold and accusing. Belle and Dalan told a grieving townswoman they had killed the creature but could not say the victims had dissolved into dust, and the party returned to Aegis City, where Max's letter from Tobias confirmed their promotion to B-rank. Max then brought Belle, Dalan, and Riyo to the Nightriver estate, where the butler informed him his father was in his study, and his guests settled in with rough gratitude, unease, and watchful refusal.

The party is fighting the undead creature and its shamblers in the vaulted hall, and must destroy their brains to put them down. — Max Nightriver and Naomi met Baroness Serenola in Driftmere, where she revealed that a mining expedition in Wendhope had vanished and that House Nightriver had ignored her letters, so Naomi joined Max's party and they went to the Minotaur's Tusk, where the survivor Garreth described tunnels that moved like living things and something ancient breathing in the dark. After an old dwarf warned that Filwern's silence meant something else had awakened, Max ordered Belle, Dalan, and Naomi to gear up, and the party descended the north shaft at first light, reaching a vast vaulted hall where a pale, eyeless figure in a miner's tunic emerged with three shambling shapes and claimed Garreth's crew now belonged to it. Dalan's arrows failed to stop the undead, so he called for the party to aim for the head and destroy the brain, and Belle's greataxe Cleaver destroyed one shambler's upper torso while Dalan put down another with an arrow through the base of the skull, leaving three undead standing as the deep breathing grew louder and something else lurked in the tunnel.

The party must finish the two remaining shamblers and the boss-thing before the unseen breathing thing in the tunnel reaches them. — Max Nightriver and Naomi met Baroness Serenola in Driftmere, learned of a vanished mining expedition in Wendhope, and heard survivor Garreth describe living tunnels and an ancient breathing thing in the dark before the party descended the North shaft at first light. In an impossibly large vaulted hall, a gaunt undead creature in a shredded miner's tunic, flanked by three shamblers, claimed Garreth's crew belonged to it, and though Dalan's arrows failed, Belle's greataxe Cleaver destroyed one shambler as Max ordered Belle to the front, Naomi behind her with Nispelheim, and Dalan to cover them while they advanced slowly. The party still had to finish the two remaining shamblers and the boss-thing before the unseen breathing thing in the tunnel reached them.

The armored figure with the single yellow eye waits in the vast cavern below the ledge, calling Max another Nightriver and saying he is early, and must be faced. — Max Nightriver and Naomi met Baroness Serenola in Driftmere, who revealed that a mining expedition in Wendhope had vanished and that House Nightriver had ignored her letters, so Naomi joined Max's party and they learned from the survivor Garreth at the Minotaur's Tusk that tunnels moved like living things and something ancient breathed in the dark. Garreth explained his crew vanished on level three of the North shaft, and after an old dwarf warned that Filwern's silence meant something else had awakened, Max ordered Belle, Dalan, and Naomi to gear up for a descent at first light. In the mines, the party reached an impossibly large vaulted hall bearing a carving of a robed figure with a twisted scepter, where a gaunt undead creature in a shredded miner's tunic emerged with three shamblers and claimed Garreth's crew now belonged to it. Belle destroyed one shambler's upper torso with Cleaver, Dalan put down others with arrows through the neck and skull, and Naomi wielded the fiery longsword Nispelheim in the Moonlight Blade style, leaving two shamblers and the boss-thing remaining as the deep breathing grew louder.

The scrap-and-bone creature with the anchor-chain is still fighting despite its destroyed core and must be put down. — Max Nightriver and Naomi joined Baroness Serenola in Driftmere after she revealed a vanished mining expedition in Wendhope, and with Garreth's account of living tunnels and an ancient presence, the party descended into the mine alongside Belle and Dalan. In a vast carved hall they destroyed an eyeless undead leader and its shamblers, though the bodies bore no crew badges, and a deeper voice taunted the Nightriver blood before they reached the second level, where a black-armored figure with a single glowing yellow eye awaited them. Following heavy breathing and metal grinding through a narrowing tunnel, Max dimmed the lantern and crept toward a bend with Belle ready and Dalan's bow aimed at the flickering yellow light.

Garreth explained that his crew vanished on level three of the North shaft, and after an old dwarf warned that Filwern's silence meant something else had awakened, Max ordered Belle, Dalan, and Naomi to gear up for a descent at first light. In the mine, the party destroyed an eyeless undead leader and its shamblers, though the bodies held no crew badges, and a deeper voice taunted the Nightriver blood before they descended to the second level, where Dalan's count put their descent near five hundred feet and the geography failed to match the Guild maps. Following heavy breathing and a flickering yellow light, Max dimmed the lantern and crept toward a bend with Belle and Dalan ready to strike, and the tunnel opened onto a ledge overlooking a vast cavern where a figure in black plate armor with a single glowing yellow eye and a jagged spear recognized Max as a Nightriver and said he was early.

The party must decide whether to break Filwern's seal, now knowing it holds Tzarak out rather than in. — The party descended through the Driftmere Mines, where Max Nightriver, Belle, Dalan, and Naomi defeated a scrap-and-bone creature and Max invited Riyo, a non-Guild fighter hiding in a side passage, to join them. Following Riyo deeper, they found ancient carvings naming Tzarak and a glyph-covered seal that Dalan read as holding back the Unspoken Breath, revealing the seal kept Tzarak from ascending rather than trapping it within. When a gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanded the seal be broken, Belle cut it down while Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering that healed the seal, only for Max to shatter it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. They emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern of suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them.

The robed creature is mid-fight on the ledge and must be stopped before it can touch Filwern's seal. — Max Nightriver and his companions—Belle, Dalan, Naomi, and the newly recruited Riyo—fought their way through the Driftmere Mines, destroying a scrap-and-bone creature and following ancient carvings toward a vast descent where something climbed an iron chain from below. At a sealed stone wall covered in pulsing glyphs, Max ordered Dalan to decipher the markings, and Dalan determined the seal held back the Unspoken Breath, with the name Tzarak repeated below, revealing that the seal kept Tzarak from ascending. Belle realized they stood before the cage of the very creature they sought, and as metallic scraping echoed from the chain below, she readied Cleaver and vowed to bury it in stone.

The party must learn whether the offering has truly appeased or sealed Filwern's wall, and what the golden light means for the seal's purpose. — The party descended through the Driftmere Mines, where Max Nightriver, Belle, Dalan, and Naomi defeated a scrap-and-bone creature and Max invited Riyo, a non-Guild fighter hiding in a side passage, to join them. Following ancient carvings that named Tzarak and spoke of an ascension, they reached a sealed, glyph-etched wall that Dalan determined held back the Unspoken Breath and kept Tzarak from ascending. When a gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanding the seal be broken, Belle cut it down while Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering of bread, salt, and a candle that healed the seal, only for Max to shatter it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. They then emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern of suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them.

The party is now inside the frozen domain past the seal, facing the vast yellow eye, and must decide how to approach or fight it. — The party descended through the Driftmere Mines, where they destroyed a scrap-and-bone creature, and Max Nightriver invited Riyo to join them despite her not being part of their Guild. Deeper down, Dalan read ancient carvings and a glyph-seal naming Tzarak and the Unspoken Breath, revealing the seal kept Tzarak from ascending. When a gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanding the seal be broken, Belle cut it down while Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering that healed the seal, only to shatter it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. The party has blinded Tzarak's eye-spot and must now press the attack before the creature recovers or retaliates. — Max Nightriver and his companions descended through the Driftmere Mines, defeating a scrap-and-bone creature and gaining Riyo as a companion, then followed ancient carvings that named Tzarak and spoke of an ascension. At a sealed, glyph-etched wall, Dalan read that the seal held back the Unspoken Breath and kept Tzarak from ascending, while something climbed the lift chain from below. A gaunt, robed creature mimicking Riyo's voice demanded the seal be broken so Tzarak could ascend, and Belle cut it down while Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering that healed the seal, only to shatter it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. They emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern of suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them.

Baroness Serenola demands to know whether the missing miners are still alive, and the party must answer for the dust that was all that remained of them. — Baroness Serenola demanded to know whether the missing miners were still alive, and the party descended into the Driftmere Mines to answer for the dust that was all that remained of them. After defeating a scrap-and-bone creature and gaining Riyo as a companion, Max Nightriver, Belle, Dalan, and Naomi followed ancient carvings naming Tzarak to a sealed, glyph-etched wall that Dalan read as holding back the Unspoken Breath and keeping Tzarak from ascending. A gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanding the seal be broken, and though Belle cut it down and Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering that healed the seal, Max shattered it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. They emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern of suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them.

The party must still find Serenola's missing people — or explain that the Devourer's death dissolved them rather than saved them. — Max Nightriver and his companions descended through the Driftmere Mines with Riyo, defeating a scrap-and-bone creature and reading ancient carvings that named Tzarak and the ascension, until they reached a sealed, glyph-etched wall holding back the Unspoken Breath. Dalan determined the seal kept Tzarak from ascending, and Riyo revealed that Tzarak was not a person but a key made of shadow and hunger, and that the seal held it out rather than in. When a gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanding the seal be broken, Belle cut it down while Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering that healed the seal, only to shatter it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. They emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern filled with suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them, leaving Serenola's missing people still unfound and the question of whether the Devourer's death dissolved them or saved them unresolved.

The party has told Driftmere what the descent cost; the wider consequences of breaking Filwern's seal and killing the creature remain to be seen. — The party descended into the mine tunnels, where they defeated a scrap-and-bone creature and Max Nightriver invited Riyo, a non-Guild fighter, to join them, then learned from ancient carvings that the floors were domains of Floor Bosses awaiting an "ascension" tied to the name Tzarak. At a ledge above a breathing darkness, Dalan read a glyph-seal older than dwarven and determined it held back the Unspoken Breath and kept Tzarak from ascending, while Riyo revealed that Tzarak was not a person but a key made of shadow and hunger, and that the seal held it out rather than in. A gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanded the seal be broken so the key could ascend, and Belle cut it down as Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering of bread, salt, and a candle that healed the seal. Max then shattered the seal with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below, and the party emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern of suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them, leaving the wider consequences of breaking Filwern's seal and killing the creature yet to be seen.

The party must return to the Aegis City Guild Hall to claim their B-rank promotion badge and rewards. — Max Nightriver ordered Dalan to read the glyphs on a seal, which revealed it held back the Unspoken Breath and kept Tzarak from ascending, and when a gaunt robed creature climbed the lift chain demanding the seal be broken, Belle cut it down while Max made a Driftmere shrine offering of bread, salt, and a candle that healed the seal before he shattered it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. Beyond the seal the party entered a frozen, glass-floored cavern filled with suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened and fixed on them, and they crossed the black glass to confront it: Max blinded it with fire, Dalan shot its eye-spot, Belle struck with Cleaver, and Max drove a lance of flame into the wound, killing the creature and freeing the suspended souls as Riyo confirmed she was unharmed and the breathing had stopped. The party climbed back to Driftmere, where Baroness Serenola received the news that the crew was gone but the creature was dead, and when Max revealed he had never seen the three letters she sent to House Nightriver, her tone turned cold and accusing as a grieving townswoman approached asking about the mine. Belle and Dalan told the woman they had killed the creature that took the missing people, though they could not bring themselves to say the victims had dissolved into dust, and the party returned to Aegis City, where Max Nightriver's letter from Tobias confirmed their promotion to B-rank for clearing the Driftmere Mines, and at the Nightriver estate the butler greeted Max and informed him his father was in his study.

Dalan drew his bow and whispered that something was waiting for them, noting the sound of metal and that the light was not a lantern. Max Nightriver dimmed the lantern and crept toward the bend, directing Belle to wait for his signal and Dalan to aim at the yellow light. Belle gripped Cleaver in tense silence, coiled and ready, while Dalan pressed against the tunnel wall with his bow drawn and whispered that he was ready. The moment was taut with anticipation as the three prepared to strike. Max Nightriver and his companions descended through the mine's lower floors, following Riyo past ancient carvings that spoke of an ascension tied to the name Tzarak. At a ledge overlooking a vast, breathing darkness, they found an old lift and a sealed stone wall covered in glowing glyphs, while something began climbing the chain from below. Output one line per change, at most 4:
[enable] <#number or entry title>
[disable] <#number or entry title>
[rewrite] <#number or entry title> || <the full replacement text>
[patch] <#number or entry title> || <first words of the span to replace> || <last words of that span> || <replacement text>
Then one final line: [why] <one sentence on what changed in the story that made these necessary>
RULES:
- Name each entry by its #number, or by its title exactly as listed above. Anything else is discarded.
- [enable] only an entry marked [currently off]; every other entry is already on.
- [disable] only an entry that is not marked [currently off].
- An entry marked [shown in part — patch only] may only be patched: you have not seen all of it.
- Some entries carry `{{// ...}}` bookkeeping markers. Never write, move or delete a marker, and never change the words between `{{// so:protect}}` and `{{// so:end}}`.
- Prefer [patch] over [rewrite]: quote the first and last words of the span exactly as they appear in the content.
- Keep replacement text under 600 characters. Never restate the whole entry in a patch.
- Only propose a change the story has actually made necessary. Style preferences are not changes.
- Never invent new entries, never touch anything outside the list, never write about the player's own knowledge.
If nothing needs changing, output NONE. That is the expected answer most of the time.

driver.recentChat:
*Javon's scarred cheek twitches. He doesn't flinch at the mention of the Witch King's name, though the air in the study seems to grow colder, as if a window has been left open to an autumn night.* "The seals are not *under* this house," *he corrects, his voice flat and precise.* "They are *in* it. In us. Each child of the Nightriver bloodline carries a seal in their very essence—a binding that keeps a great evil dormant. When the bloodline ends, the seals break, and He Who Curses awakens once more."
*He turns his head slightly, glancing toward the window and the grounds beyond.* "The Witch King is not a legend, Max. He is a prison. And you, Natalia, and Welden are his jailers. Your blood is the key that keeps him in shadow." *His green eyes snap back to Max, hard as emeralds.* "This is why the marriages are not merely political. This is why Natalia and Welden are being wed to houses that can strengthen our line, ensuring the seals hold for another generation."
*He straightens his back, his tall frame imposing in the dim light.* "You would break the line, would you not? You would see the Witch King rise again? Or perhaps you believe you can end the burden without ending the blood."

[Earlier scenes]
In the marble foyer of the estate, Max Nightriver asked Belle if she remembered Garreth, the survivor from the Minotaur's Tusk, and what he had told them about the mines. Belle's brow furrowed as she reached back to the dim tavern and the smell of damp wool, the scene tense with the weight of memory.
Welden arrived in the library, more jumpy than usual, and refused to explain the reason for his unease. The scene carried a tense, uneasy mood as his unexplained agitation went unaddressed.
Max Nightriver went to Father's study, where Lord Javon Nightriver confronted him about his conduct after clearing the Driftmere Mines. When Max asked whether Baroness Serenola's three letters had reached the house, Javon replied that her pleas were handled and that nothing in the house was done without purpose. The scene was tense and guarded, with Javon cold and unreadable.

[The story so far]
The Adventurer's Guild: The party advanced down a twisting tunnel where the walls closed in, damp and smelling of wet stone and old blood. The heavy breathing they had followed changed into rhythmic metal grinding, and a yellow light flickered at the bend ahead. Dalan drew his bow and whispered that something was waiting for them, noting the sound of metal and that the light was not a lantern. Max Nightriver dimmed the lantern and crept toward the bend, directing Belle to wait for his signal and Dalan to aim at the yellow light. Belle gripped Cleaver in tense silence, coiled and ready, while Dalan pressed against the tunnel wall with his bow drawn and whispered that he was ready. The moment was taut with anticipation as the three prepared to strike. Max Nightriver and his companions descended through the mine's lower floors, following Riyo past ancient carvings that spoke of an ascension tied to the name Tzarak. At a ledge overlooking a vast, breathing darkness, they found an old lift and a sealed stone wall covered in glowing glyphs, while something began climbing the chain from below. The tone was tense and foreboding as the party confronted the hungry, nameless presence awaiting them. Max Nightriver ordered Dalan to read the glyphs on a seal and reveal what was locked behind it and…

- Javon has set three conditions Max must meet before he will reveal the truth of the house's seals and marriages — whether Max meets them, and what the truth is, is unresolved.
- Javon's stated purpose for 'handling' Serenola's letters remains unexplained — who ordered it and why is unresolved.
- Javon suspects Max has been receiving letters he knows nothing about — who is writing to Max, and what Javon will do about it, is unresolved.
- Welden is in the library, jumpier than usual and refusing to explain what troubles him.

Max Nightriver dimmed the lantern and crept toward the bend, directing Belle to wait for his signal and Dalan to aim at the yellow light. At a ledge overlooking a vast, breathing darkness, they found an old lift and a sealed stone wall covered in glowing glyphs, while something began climbing the chain from below. The tone was tense and foreboding as the party confronted the hungry, nameless presence awaiting them. 115.text: Remembered: A grieving townsfolk woman whose son did not return from the mine approached the party on the road outside Driftmere, asking if they had gone in.
Remembered: Dalan told the woman the mine is free but could not bring himself to say the missing people dissolved into glittering dust when the monster fell.
Remembered: Dalan told the woman the party searched every reachable tunnel and that the thing that took the miners is gone.
New thread: The grieving townsfolk mother whose son died in the mine now knows the party killed the thing that took him — whether she accepts their account or demands more remains open.

117.text: Remembered: The party has been raised to B-rank for clearing the Driftmere Mines and must return to the Aegis City Guild Hall to claim the promotion badge and rewards.
Remembered: Max has returned to the Nightriver estate and been told his father is waiting in his study.
Remembered: The butler told Max his father is in his study.
Remembered: The butler tells Max his father is in his study upon his return home.
New thread: Max has been summoned to his father's study at the Nightriver estate — what Lord Javon wants is unknown.

118.text: Remembered: Belle, Dalan, Naomi and Riyo have been brought to the Nightriver estate as Max's guests.

119.text: New thread: The party must return to the Aegis City Guild Hall to claim their B-rank promotion badge and rewards.

120.text: Thread resolved: The party must return to the Aegis City Guild Hall to claim their B-rank promotion badge and rewards.
New thread: Baroness Serenola waits in her study to speak about House Nightriver, and Max has sworn to learn whether the house received and discarded her three letters.

121.text: Home for the Recess: Home for the mid-year recess, the estate is quieter than it should be, and the family is not quite as you left it.
Remembered: Riyo refuses a room at the estate and insists on waiting by the door, positioning herself between Max and the rest of the estate.
New thread: The party has been promoted to B-rank and must return to the Aegis City Guild Hall to claim the badge and rewards.

123.text: Remembered: Belle recounts Garreth's account: the tunnels moved and were alive, and he heard his crew calling for him in the dark before he ran.
Remembered: Belle confirms the party broke the healed seal with Max's fire, went through, and killed Tzarak, freeing the frozen dead.
New thread: Riyo's refusal of a room and her guarded vigil by the estate door — what she is hiding and why she will not settle in.

124.text: Remembered: Welden appears in the estate library, unusually jumpy, and refuses to say why.
New thread: Welden is behaving strangely and refuses to explain what is troubling him.

126.text: Remembered: Lord Javon holds a letter bearing an unfamiliar wax seal — a simple crest of a grain stalk — and confronts Max about letters sent to the house.
Remembered: Javon tells Max the Guild reported the party cleared the Driftmere Mines and that his conduct afterward is what brings them to this conversation.
New thread: Javon has confronted Max about letters sent to the house, holding a letter with a grain-stalk seal — what he knows about Serenola's three unanswered letters is unresolved.

128.text: Remembered: Lord Javon admits Serenola's letters reached the estate and were deliberately 'handled' — nothing in the house is done without purpose.
Remembered: Javon admits the estate deliberately 'handled' Serenola's letters, saying nothing in the house is done without purpose.
New thread: Javon has admitted the estate deliberately 'handled' Serenola's letters — what that purpose was, and who ordered it, is unresolved.
New thread: Welden is in the library, jumpier than usual and refusing to explain what troubles him.

130.text: Remembered: Javon holds a letter bearing a grain-stalk seal and confronts Max about letters he suspects Max has been receiving.
Remembered: Javon summoned Max because he went to the mines instead of preparing for court, signed a Guild register, and brought outsiders into the house.
Remembered: Javon holds a letter bearing a grain-stalk seal and confronts Max about letters Max has been receiving that Javon knows nothing about.
Remembered: Javon summoned Max because he went to the mines instead of preparing for court, signed the Guild register, and brought outsiders into the house.
Remembered: Javon dismisses the dead miners as a drop in the ocean amid the Darran Kingdom's war.
Remembered: Javon suspects Max has been receiving letters he knows nothing about.
New thread: Javon suspects Max has been receiving letters he knows nothing about — who is writing to Max, and what Javon will do about it, is unresolved.
New thread: Javon's stated purpose for 'handling' Serenola's letters remains unexplained — who ordered it and why is unresolved.

132.text: Remembered: Javon sets three conditions before revealing the truth of the house: explain the conduct at the mines, name the source of Serenola's story, and understand some questions must wait until Max is strong enough.

Remembered: Javon sets three conditions before revealing the truth of the house: Max must explain his conduct at the mines, tell him who Serenola's story came from, and understand some questions must wait until he is strong enough.
New thread: Javon has set three conditions Max must meet before he will reveal the truth of the house's seals and marriages — whether Max meets them, and what the truth is, is unresolved.

134.text: Remembered: Javon reveals the seals are not under the house but in the Nightriver bloodline itself: each child carries a binding that keeps a great evil dormant, and when the bloodline ends the seals break and He Who Curses awakens.
Remembered: Javon states the Witch King is a prison, and Max, Natalia and Welden are his jailers, their blood the key that keeps him in shadow.
Remembered: Javon explains the marriages are meant to strengthen the Nightriver line so the seals hold another generation.
New thread: The truth of the Nightriver seals and the Witch King — Max now knows the bloodline is the prison, but how to act on it, and what Javon's three conditions will reveal, is unresolved.
